Burzenin Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Witów, Poland

Demolished. Burzenin, a former town founded before 1378 and downgraded in 1870, recorded its first Jews in 1764; population reached 49.5% (383) by 1859, settling at 19.9% (228) by 1921. Until 1812, this cemetery also served nearby Sieradz's Jews, who had no burial ground of their own; the local kehilla itself remained under Sieradz county's jurisdiction until forming independently in the 19th century. Following the September 1939 German occupation, residents were transported to the Zduńska Wola and Pabianice ghettos, then to Chełmno.
